name: slot-pin-move-on-amendment
description:
Single-occupancy pinning, end to end through the plan gate: the agent is cleared for repo-alpha, then re-plans the SAME phase to point at repo-bravo, and the second card is a MOVE.

code_repo is session-only, so the first approval BINDS and therefore PINS repo-alpha (a non-expiring slot_pin tuple), and the first codepin_fetch(repo-alpha) succeeds on the grant that approval wrote. The re-plan re-points the phase's one slot to repo-bravo: same handle, same budget, so nothing widens but the instance. That arrives as a plan_amendment (DiffPhase finds the slot value changed), and because the session is already pinned to repo-alpha the amendment card is a MOVE — it names BOTH instances (repo-alpha → repo-bravo) and says in words that approving moves the pin and revokes this session's access to repo-alpha. Approving it repoints the pin and revokes repo-alpha's grant in one request, so the second codepin_fetch(repo-bravo) then succeeds on the moved grant.

cardWhatContains asserts the move copy, not just the two ids: a card that rendered repo-bravo as a plain first-fill would hide the revocation the approval comes with, and a bare-ids assertion would pass it (repo-alpha appears on the first card regardless). The category stays plan_amendment (the spec decision — no new interaction kind for a move), so autoApprove clears it exactly as it clears the first phase.

The companion slot_pinning e2e scenario asserts the same pin/move at the SpiceDB-tuple level (slot_pin present, the read grant moving off repo-alpha onto repo-bravo) and proves the ErrSlotPinned refusal text for both rebind modes; this bundle proves the move renders on a REAL published card driven by a real model script. approvalPrompts is 2 and WHICH two is the point: one plan_phase for repo-alpha, one plan_amendment MOVE for repo-bravo.

cardWhatContains: revokes this session's access to repo-alpha
